title: US relentless in pursuing extradition of Apollo Quiboloy, says PH ambassador
summary: The US government will be relentless in pursuing the extradition of Filipino religious leader Apollo Quiboloy, who is facing trafficking charges in California, Philippine Ambassador to the United…

blocks.text: The US government will be relentless in pursuing the extradition of Filipino religious leader Apollo Quiboloy, who is facing trafficking charges in California, Philippine Ambassador to the United States Babes Romualdez said on Tuesday.
In an interview with "Balitanghali," Romualdez said the US is keen to bring in Quiboloy.

“The court is going to be the one to make the decision on the extradition case. The US is of course very interested to bring Pastor Quiboloy into justice because he has many supposed crime committed in the United States,” Romualdez said.
“Hindi nila pakakawalan ‘yan. They really want to make sure that he will be tried in the US to the crimes that he committed there,” Romualdez added.
(They will no longer let this go.)

The Department of Justice (DOJ) announced on November 12 that the Makati Regional Trial Court issued an extradition arrest warrant and hold-departure order for Quiboloy and two of his co-accused, Teresita Tolibas Dandan and Helen Panilag, in connection with their charges of international human trafficking, sex trafficking, conspiracy, and bulk cash smuggling.
The court issued the arrest warrant based on the DOJ’s extradition petition for Quiboloy and two of his co-accused, which the DOJ filed on behalf of the US government.

The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Monday said it is ready to assist in the possible extradition of Quiboloy, the leader of the Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KOJC) religious group. –Llanesca T. Panti/NB, GMA News
